# When REITs Trade 20% Below Their Value, They Usually Win Big: Tickeron AI's 10 Deepest-Discount REITs, Buy or Sell

**Data as of October 6, 2026 (intraday)**

# Key Takeaways

* **History says deep discounts pay.** Janus Henderson's study (1990 to September 2022) found that after public REITs traded at a 20% or greater discount to net asset value (NAV), they returned 30.1% in the following year, 56.3% over two years and 89.0% over three. Private real estate lost money over the same windows.
* **Public REITs beat private real estate 100% of the time** over every two- and three-year period that followed, and in 86% of one-year periods.
* **The discount is back.** The median REIT NAV discount widened from -9.44% to -15.13% during August, and small-cap REITs now average -24.26% ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4948460-the-state-of-reits-september-2026-edition)). The FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs Index then fell 5.7% in September ([Nareit](https://www.reit.com/data-research)).
* **Tickeron AI's 10 deepest-discount REITs:** 9 of the 10 trade at 20% or more below book value, led by[ MPT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MPT/) (56.4% below book),[ ARE](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ARE/) (48.5%) and[ RYN](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RYN/) (46.3%).
* **Verdict: 5 BUYS, 5 SELLS.** BUY:[ RITM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RITM/),[ MRP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRP/),[ RYN](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RYN/),[ ARE](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ARE/),[ PDM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PDM/). SELL:[ MPT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MPT/),[ KRC](https://tickeron.com/ticker/KRC/),[ IIPR](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IIPR/),[ RLJ](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RLJ/),[ DEA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/DEA/). A deep discount only pays if the business behind it is stable.
* **Tickeron has built Financial Learning Models (FLMs) and** [**AI Trading Bots**](https://tickeron.com/app/ai-robots/trending-robots/) **for all 10 REITs.** The FLMs read each stock's trend, and the Bots weigh rotation across real estate sub-sectors, from office and healthcare to timber and hotels.

# What Is a "Discount to NAV"? A Retail Investor's Guide

**NAV (net asset value)** is what a REIT's buildings are worth at today's private-market prices, minus its debt, per share. When a REIT's stock trades below NAV, you are buying its real estate for less than a private buyer would pay.

**Why discounts close:**

* Private buyers (like Blackstone) acquire discounted REITs outright.
* Management buys back cheap stock or sells assets at full value.
* Or the stock simply re-rates when interest rates stabilize.

**Our proxy: price-to-book.** Consensus NAV estimates from Green Street and other providers are behind paywalls. So we screened every US equity REIT worth more than $1 billion by price-to-book: market value divided by shareholders' equity on the latest balance sheet (June 30, 2026). Book value is usually conservative for REITs, because buildings are carried at their depreciated cost. A stock below book is often trading below NAV too, but not always. Office and healthcare buildings with falling values can have a NAV below book.

# Group 1: Healthcare and Life-Science Real Estate ([**MPT**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MPT/),[ **ARE**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ARE/))

[**MPT**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MPT/) **(Medical Properties Trust) — SELL. 1-month forecast: DOWN.** The deepest discount on the list (56.4% below book) is a value trap: the stock is near its $3.21 low, and half of recent analysts are bearish given its long-running hospital-tenant problems.

[**ARE**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ARE/) **(Alexandria Real Estate Equities) — BUY. 1-month forecast: UP.** Alexandria trades at nearly half of book value (0.52x) while holding its $0.72 quarterly dividend ([Alexandria IR](https://investor.are.com/news-events-and-webcasts/news/news-details/2026/Alexandria-Real-Estate-Equities-Inc--Declares-Cash-Dividend-of-0-72-per-Common-Share-for-3Q26/default.aspx)), the classic setup the Janus chart describes, with +16.5% to target.

# Group 2: Land, Timber and Housing Capital ([**RYN**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RYN/),[ **MRP**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRP/))

[**RYN**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RYN/) **(Rayonier) — BUY. 1-month forecast: UP.** After its merger with PotlatchDeltic created a timberland owner with over four million acres ([Rayonier IR](https://ir.rayonier.com/news/news-details/2026/Rayonier-and-PotlatchDeltic-Announce-Closing-of-Merger-of-Equals/default.aspx)), Rayonier trades 46.3% below book with +34.9% to target and no bearish analysts.

[**MRP**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRP/) **(Millrose Properties) — BUY. 1-month forecast: UP.** At 0.61x book, this homebuilder land-banking REIT offers the biggest upside on the list (+68.3%), though a fresh downgrade by Citizens ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRP/)) makes it a higher-risk buy.

# Group 3: Office ([**KRC**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/KRC/),[ **PDM**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PDM/),[ **DEA**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/DEA/))

[**KRC**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/KRC/) **(Kilroy Realty) — SELL. 1-month forecast: DOWN.** The 24.3% discount reflects real West Coast office risk, and only 12% of recent analysts are bullish.

[**PDM**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PDM/) **(Piedmont Office Realty) — BUY. 1-month forecast: UP.** Piedmont is 23.3% below book and only 11% off its high, with +18.2% to target and no bearish analysts: the office name where the trend is already turning.

[**DEA**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/DEA/) **(Easterly Government Properties) — SELL. 1-month forecast: DOWN.** The government tenants are safe, but at 18.1% below book Easterly misses the 20% threshold, and with only +4.9% to target and no bullish analysts there is little catalyst.

# Group 4: Specialty and Hotels ([**RITM**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RITM/),[ **IIPR**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IIPR/),[ **RLJ**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RLJ/))

[**RITM**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RITM/) **(Rithm Capital) — BUY. 1-month forecast: UP.** Every recent analyst is bullish, and the $13.12 average target implies +51.5% from a stock trading at 0.57x book.

[**IIPR**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IIPR/) **(Innovative Industrial Properties) — SELL. 1-month forecast: DOWN.** The cannabis-property landlord is cheap (0.78x book), but with only +1.5% to target and its only recent rating a Strong Sell, tenant risk outweighs the discount.

[**RLJ**](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RLJ/) **(RLJ Lodging Trust) — SELL. 1-month forecast: DOWN.** The hotel REIT trades 21.2% below book, but half of recent analysts are bearish and only +3.6% remains to target.

**The lesson:** the Janus chart measures the whole REIT market, not single stocks. A diversified basket bought at a 20% discount has historically won. Individual REITs at deep discounts can stay cheap, or get cheaper, if tenants are failing. Our BUYS combine a deep discount with analyst support. Our SELLS have deep discounts but weak analyst conviction or heavy tenant risk.

 

# How Tickeron's FLMs and AI Trading Bots Cover All 10

[**Tickeron**](https://tickeron.com/) **has created a Financial Learning Model (FLM) for every REIT in this report:**[ MPT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MPT/),[ ARE](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ARE/),[ RYN](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RYN/),[ RITM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RITM/),[ MRP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRP/),[ KRC](https://tickeron.com/ticker/KRC/),[ PDM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PDM/),[ IIPR](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IIPR/),[ RLJ](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RLJ/) and[ DEA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/DEA/). Each FLM learns its stock's trend behavior. That separates a discounted REIT starting to turn up ([PDM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PDM/), near its high) from one still making new lows ([MPT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MPT/)).

**Tickeron also runs** [**AI Trading Bots**](https://tickeron.com/app/ai-robots/trending-robots/) **for all 10.** The Bots take the sector into account. Real estate is really a dozen different businesses, from office towers and hospitals to timberland and hotels. The Bots rotate toward the sub-sectors where the discount is starting to close, rather than buying everything that looks cheap.

**The bottom line:** history says buying REITs at a 20%+ discount has paid off handsomely over one to three years. The skill is picking which discounts close, and the FLMs and Bots are built for exactly that.

comments.body: The post is upfront that price-to-book is only a proxy for NAV, and that matters here: the Janus result is for a diversified basket measured against Green Street NAV, so it doesn't carry over to ten single names screened on book value, where office and healthcare names can have a NAV below book. The BUY/SELL calls would also be easier to judge with a dated record of past calls and what happened to them, compared against a REIT index. REITs move a lot on rate expectations, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for CPI, FOMC and other macro releases) is one source for checking how much of a discount's "closing" came from rate days.
